title: React Data Fetching Applied Check
description: Apply data-fetching knowledge to race conditions, loading states, fetch and Axios behavior, query keys, cancellation, cache invalidation, and optimistic updates.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A component runs `useEffect(() => { fetchUser(userId); }, [])` and `userId` can change. What is the main bug?

options.text: The effect will refetch too often
The effect may keep showing data for the first `userId` because the dependency is missing
The fetch request cannot return JSON
The component will never mount

questions.explanation: Values used by an effect should usually appear in its dependency array. Otherwise the request can become stale when props or state change.

questions.prompt: Two searches are triggered quickly: request A for `rea`, then request B for `react`. A resolves last and overwrites B. What is the best fix?

options.text: Track or cancel stale requests so only the latest result updates state
Move the fetch into the JSX
Ignore errors from both requests
Use array indexes as keys

questions.explanation: Race conditions happen when older requests finish after newer ones. AbortController, request ids, or a query library can prevent stale writes.

questions.prompt: Which UI choices are better than a spinner-only interface? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Show useful empty states
Preserve previous data during background refresh when appropriate
Provide retry actions for recoverable failures
Hide all existing content on every refetch

questions.explanation: Good request UIs distinguish initial loading from background refresh and provide recovery paths instead of blanking everything repeatedly.

questions.prompt: Given `const key = ['todos']` for both `/todos?status=open` and `/todos?status=done`, what is likely to happen?

options.text: The cache may mix different filtered results because the filter is not in the key
React will automatically create two caches
The queries will always be disabled
The HTTP method changes to POST

questions.explanation: Query keys should include variables that change the returned data, such as filters, ids, search terms, and pagination inputs.

questions.prompt: An optimistic todo add appears in the list, then the mutation fails. What should the app normally do?

options.text: Keep the optimistic item forever
Rollback or mark the optimistic item as failed, and communicate the error
Reload the entire browser tab immediately
Delete the entire cache

questions.explanation: Optimistic updates need a failure path. The app should restore the previous state or clearly show that the pending change failed.

questions.prompt: In SWR, why might a key be `null`, as in `useSWR(userId ? ['/api/user', userId] : null, fetcher)`?

options.text: To conditionally skip fetching until required input exists
To force an infinite retry loop
To disable React rendering
To make the response uncachable

questions.explanation: SWR treats a null key as disabled, which is useful when a request depends on data that is not available yet.

questions.prompt: An error boundary is enough by itself to model ordinary request failures from `fetch` in state-driven UIs.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Error boundaries catch render-time errors, not ordinary rejected promises managed inside effects. Request errors should be represented in UI state or handled by a query library.

questions.prompt: A component passes `{ page, filter }` as part of a query key but recreates the object each render. Which practice is usually clearer?

options.text: Use a stable structured key like `['items', page, filter]`
Use `Math.random()` in the key
Remove all variables from the key
Store the key in localStorage

questions.explanation: Structured keys should clearly represent data identity. Primitive segments make the key easy to reason about and avoid accidental cache misses.
